status: Proceed to previously frozen held-out cohort without changing candidate; production adoption is not authorized.
flag_interpretation: Candidate uses Phi-only with the K1 queue here (stream-worker-deficit). The recurring original-scheduler comparison is consistent with the previously observed K1 first-call tradeoff. Candidate vs phi1 is +3.91% median with mixed block directions, and phi1 vs baseline is +5.68% with mixed directions; these controls do not prove an exact causal attribution or excuse the repeatable candidate-vs-baseline regression.
matched_interpretation: Conservative fallback deliberately gives up favorable streaming: at matched Meissel/2threads it is +111.90% first and +12.02% warm vs common-K1 v2. For zero/2threads it is +10.10% first and +2.74% warm vs v2. All those pairs are slower in every block. Relative to phi1 these fallback paths remain close, preserving queue gains versus production.
conclusion: The focused experiment supports retaining large-input streaming and the queue improvement while protecting enlarged-table warmed calls. It does not establish a universally fastest selector, and the known first-call scheduler regression plus conservative missed opportunities remain review items. The frozen held-out cohort can test this policy without fitting away those costs.
